cause: The new evaluator's validation command used broad unittest discovery instead of naming only its two synthetic-test files.
access_description: An older test parsed the holdout manifest to check its schema and absence of surface forms. An older --status-only call also parsed the manifest and printed lock/count metadata. Another test read the lock marker. Metadata access violated the task's restricted-material boundary even though the payload was not decoded.
additional_test_execution: The broad discovery also invoked an older tokenizer diagnostic dry-run, which failed because sentencepiece was unavailable, before encoding. No new tokenizer evaluation completed. A separate old test failed on an obsolete approval-status expectation. Neither old test is being changed or rerun here.
response: Work stopped and the owner was notified. The evaluator specification commit b535f50 already existed; the audit implementation and generated reports remained uncommitted. The owner subsequently authorized incident documentation, exact-file test restriction, and completion of validation.
remediation: Replace broad discovery in the new audit's instructions and CI with exact filenames for its two synthetic-test modules.
Disclose this metadata-access exception in the audit JSON, Markdown, console summary, and research decision log.
Distinguish the fixed-input audit runner's access scope from the broader validation session's incident.
Do not reopen or hash the restricted metadata to document the incident; use only the observed test output and reviewed test/source control flow.
Preserve the original scorer, frozen development gold, policies, stored results, lambda selection, and success criteria.
scientific_scope: The reported audit scores are a post-hoc measurement audit of fixed archived development predictions. This record does not certify the broader session as free of holdout access and does not replace historical V1 outcomes.
